title: Peripheral Precocious Puberty: McCune-Albright, Testotoxicosis and Aromatase Blockade
subject: ss-paediatric-endocrinology
module: Precocious and Delayed Puberty, Hypogonadism and Gynecomastia

steps.say: Peripheral precocious puberty is characterized by autonomous sex steroid excess with suppressed pituitary gonadotropins.
steps.tx: Recognize the biochemical hallmark of a **Peripheral (GnRH-independent) pubertal signature** in symptomatic children. Peripheral precocious puberty results from autonomous sex steroid production independent of pituitary LH/FSH; serum gonadotropins remain suppressed (LH < 0.1 IU/L) even after GnRH stimulation, contrasting sharply with the pubertal LH surge of central precocity.

vis.alt: Physiological hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis diagram detailing central GnRH, LH, and FSH drive to gonads and adrenarche pathways.
vis.caption: Hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis showing the central hormonal drive that is suppressed in peripheral precocious puberty.

steps.say: McCune-Albright syndrome is a classic mosaic disorder driven by postzygotic somatic GNAS mutations.
steps.tx: Characterize the **McCune-Albright syndrome triad and somatic GNAS** mosaic mutations in affected patients. McCune-Albright syndrome is caused by postzygotic somatic mosaic activating mutations in GNAS (p.Arg201), presenting with triad of peripheral precocious puberty (large ovarian cysts), café-au-lait spots (coast of Maine), and polyostotic fibrous dysplasia.

vis.title: McCune-Albright Classical Triad (3 Components)
rows: Painless cyclic vaginal bleeding in young girls
Large, asymmetric cafe-au-lait macules with jagged edges
Polyostotic fibrous dysplasia, fractures, shepherd's crook deformity

steps.say: Autonomous ovarian cysts in McCune-Albright spontaneously form and regress, causing abrupt estrogen withdrawal bleeding.
steps.tx: Identify the clinical presentation of **Recurrent estrogenic bleeding in McCune-Albright** in young phenotypic girls. Young girls with McCune-Albright present with sudden painless vaginal bleeding from estrogen withdrawal as autonomous luteinized follicular cysts spontaneously form and regress, recurring cyclically without preceding thelarche progression.

vis.title: Estrogen Withdrawal Bleeding Cycle in MAS

nodes.label: Postzygotic GNAS Mosaic Activation in Ovary

edges: Abrupt estrogen drop induces vaginal menses

steps.say: Third-generation aromatase inhibitors combined with estrogen receptor blockers provide effective medical management.
steps.tx: Prescribe **Aromatase inhibitor and estrogen blocker therapy** to arrest skeletal and sexual advancement in girls with McCune-Albright. Medical therapy for McCune-Albright precocity utilizes third-generation aromatase inhibitors (letrozole 2.5 mg/day) combined with selective estrogen receptor modulators (tamoxifen) to arrest vaginal bleeding and skeletal maturation, with anastrozole as an alternative.

left.title: Aromatase Inhibitors
points: Blocks peripheral conversion of androgens to estrogens
Significantly slows growth velocity and bone age acceleration

right.title: Estrogen Receptor Modulators
points: Directly antagonizes estrogen action on endometrium and breast

steps.say: Testotoxicosis is a male-limited disorder driven by activating mutations in the luteinizing hormone receptor.
steps.tx: Recognize the genetics and early onset of **Familial male-limited precocious puberty (Testotoxicosis)** in boys. Testotoxicosis is an autosomal dominant condition caused by activating mutations in LHCGR (2p21), driving constitutive Leydig cell testosterone secretion in boys by age 2-4 years despite prepubertal LH, producing bilateral phallic and testicular enlargement.

vis.title: Testotoxicosis Clinical Profile
rows: Constitutive G-protein coupling in Leydig cells
Negative feedback from high circulating testosterone
Leydig cell hyperplasia without tubular maturation

steps.tx: This receptor behaves as if the pituitary were shouting when it is actually silent. A gain of function change locks the **LH receptor** on Leydig cells into its active shape, so testosterone pours out in a young boy while measured LH stays suppressed. The result is rapid growth, penile enlargement and pubic hair with testes only modestly enlarged, the signature pattern of testotoxicosis.
steps.say: An always active LH receptor drives Leydig cells to make testosterone while pituitary LH stays suppressed. That pattern produces early virilisation in testotoxicosis.

vis.alt: Testis diagram with an LH receptor locked in its active shape on Leydig cells, driving testosterone output without pituitary signal.
vis.caption: Constitutively active LH receptor in the testis causing testosterone excess in testotoxicosis. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.say: Dual therapy combining an anti-androgen with an aromatase inhibitor effectively halts virilization and epiphyseal fusion.
steps.tx: Implement protocolized **Dual-agent therapy for testotoxicosis** to preserve adult height and control virilization. Testotoxicosis is treated with an anti-androgen (bicalutamide or spironolactone) combined with an aromatase inhibitor (anastrozole or letrozole) to block androgen receptors and prevent estrogen-mediated epiphyseal closure. Regular auxological follow-up and serial bone age determinations ensure therapeutic efficacy and guide timely dosage adjustments during growth.

left.title: Anti-Androgen Component
points: Competitively blocks peripheral androgen receptor binding
Arrests rapid penile growth, pubarche, and aggressive behavior

right.title: Aromatase Inhibitor Component
points: Blocks aromatization of testosterone to estradiol
Prevents accelerated epiphyseal fusion and preserves adult height

steps.say: Prolonged exposure to peripheral sex steroids can mature the hypothalamus, triggering secondary central precocious puberty.
steps.tx: Anticipate the emergence of a **Secondary central activation phenomenon** following control of peripheral precocity. Chronic exposure to high peripheral sex steroid levels accelerates hypothalamic maturation; upon medical suppression of peripheral steroids, a secondary true central precocious puberty commonly erupts, requiring GnRH agonists such as leuprolide.

vis.title: Evolution to Secondary Central Precocious Puberty

nodes.label: Medical Suppression of Peripheral Steroid Source

edges: Advanced bone age and neuroendocrine priming

steps.say: Autonomous gonadal neoplasms must be excluded in children presenting with unilateral or rapidly progressing precocity.
steps.tx: Evaluate surgical etiologies involving **Granulosa and Leydig cell tumors** presenting with peripheral precocity. Ovarian juvenile granulosa cell tumors (producing estradiol and inhibin B) and testicular Leydig cell tumors (unilateral testicular mass, asymmetric enlargement) are surgical causes of peripheral precocity requiring urgent pelvic or scrotal ultrasonography and surgical resection.

vis.title: Gonadal Neoplasms Causing Peripheral Precocity
rows: Elevated estradiol and inhibin B; unilateral oophorectomy
High testosterone with suppressed LH; radical inguinal orchiectomy
